text:
Jin (support): FYI customer 'acme-corp' opened a ticket — p95/p99 spiked after last night's routing/config rollout. They say interactive latency for small prompts jumped from ~120ms p95 to ~450ms and p99s up to ~2.2s.
Alex (eng-sre): Thanks, can you paste the request IDs or a trace? Which model/route?
Jin (support): route=redwood.chat.standard, model=rwd-v1-small, example req-id=rid_20260312_001, attached logs show a lot of 'waiting for batch' events.
Maria (eng-runtime): @Alex I saw the config roll last night — we changed continuous_batcher.timeout_ms from 30 -> 120 for throughput tests and lowered min_batch_size to 1. That would increase hold windows for tiny requests.
Pat (eng-ml): That matches: if tiny requests are common, increasing timeout will coalesce them into larger batches which helps throughput but hurts tail latency for single-turn interactive queries.
Alex (eng-sre): Can we repro in staging? I can generate small prompt traffic at ~50rps and compare p95/p99 across configs.
Maria (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used:
```
# spawn 50 rps of 8-token prompts
ab -n 5000 -c 10 -p small_prompt.json -T application/json http://staging-infer.local/v1/generate
```
Runtime config snippet from current prod:
```
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  min_batch_size: 1
  max_batch_size: 64
  timeout_ms: 120
  max_wait_ms: 200
  prefer_latency_path: false
```
Alex (eng-sre): Ok. Logs show many requests hit the coalescing path and waited ~100-180ms before being released. That explains p95 jump.
Jin (support): Customer is on Dedicated and has an SLA — they want it fixed or rolled back.
Maria (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation options: 1) revert timeout_ms to 30 (fast rollback), 2) set prefer_latency_path: true for the route (prefer immediate dispatch for small reqs), 3) increase min_batch_size to 4 for throughput-small tradeoff (but that might worsen small single-user latency).
Pat (eng-ml): Also consider enabling small-request fast-path that bypasses continuous coalescer for token-length<=16. We have an experimental flag: `tiny_request_passthrough: true`.
Alex (eng-sre): Immediate plan: revert the config globally to previous commit for now (safer). Then roll a targeted canary: enable prefer_latency_path + tiny_request_passthrough on redwood.chat.standard for 10% traffic and monitor p95/p99 for 30m.
Maria (eng-runtime): I'll kick the rollback and open a canary config PR. Deploy-bot will post when the rollback is live.
deploy-bot: config-deploy: rollback of continuous_batcher timeout -> 30ms started (PR #4248). Canary flags available as `rbac:route:flags`
Alex (eng-sre): Support please tell customer we've rolled back and we're running a canary for latency tuning.
Jin (support): Noted, I'll update the acme ticket and offer status.
Maria (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: we should add metrics that correlate wait-time in batcher -> client latency, and add an alert when p95>200ms for interactive routes. Also we need to codify small-request fast-path for Dedicated customers with interactive SLAs.
Pat (eng-ml): I'll prototype threshold-based passthrough (prompt_tokens <= 16 -> bypass). Perf should improve without sacrificing backend throughput for bulk workloads.
Alex (eng-sre): Good. After canary, we'll run a 2-hour sustained traffic sim to ensure no regressions, then gradually re-enable optimized batching with route-level overrides.
Jin (support): Customer notified and happy with rollback for now. Keeping thread open for canary results. :thumbsup:
Maria (eng-runtime): Canary metrics after 10m: p95 dropped back to ~130ms, p99 ~480ms (improved). Will report again at 30m.
Alex (eng-sre): Nice. Leave monitoring on, and if p99 stays <600ms we can consider permanent route flag.
Pat (eng-ml): Note: long-term we should expose these knobs in Console per-route so customers can opt-in for latency vs cost.
Jin (support): Closing loop with acme once canary stable.
Alex (eng-sre): Thanks everyone.
